task_definition.task_name: DAS Wavefield Decomposition using Curvelet Windowing

task_description.overview: Decompose the DAS wavefield by apparent velocity using a curvelet‐based filter.
steps: Load the preprocessed DAS waveform matrix with metadata.
Apply fast discrete curvelet transform to the time–distance data.
Define a velocity threshold (vmin) to separate components.
Window curvelet coefficients corresponding to velocities above and below vmin.
Perform inverse curvelet transform to reconstruct separated wavefields.

task_definition.agent_prompt: Use the curvelet_windowing method to decompose the DAS waveform data ({waveform_data_path}) with channel spacing of 8 m and sampling rate of 250 Hz. Perform the `spike_removal` and `channel_checking(use=True)` on the loaded daspy section object. Then, perform `curvelet_windowing(mode='decompose', vmin=1000)` to decompose the wavefield into two separated wavefields: one containing seismic waves and the other containing traffic signals. Finally, plot a figure (1x3) to show the waveform (original waveform, the separated seismic component, the separated traffic component). Note: try to use daspy package to load, process and visualize the data. 2) Save the decomposed earthquake data to {decomposed_earthquake_data} and the decomposed traffic data to {decomposed_traffic_data} and save the plot to {decomposed_plot}.
